concerns.concern: The contacts are not shown to be ballistic or spectroscopic. No normal-state contact resistance, Wexler/Sharvin contact radius or contact-size-to-mean-free-path ratio is reported, and numbers in Fig. 2 are unexplained. Checks are requested that structure vanishes at bulk Tc and that raw G(V) above Tc is shown.
concerns.quote: No normal-state contact resistance R_N is reported for any S1 spectrum. There is no Wexler/Sharvin estimate of the contact radius and no a/l ratio.

concerns.concern: Side dips are a known critical-current or heating artifact of non-ballistic contacts, yet they are used as intrinsic evidence of nodes and of the ABS. Measurements on several contacts with varied R_N, tracking dip position against R_N, T and H, are needed.
concerns.quote: Dips whose position scales with R_N or with Jc(T, H) are artifacts. If this test cannot be done, side dips should be removed as evidence of nodes.

concerns.concern: All pressure data come from one sample and possibly one contact, whose Z and Γ change strongly with pressure. The trends may reflect contact reconstruction or freezing of the pressure medium rather than intrinsic changes. Further crystals and contacts and a pressure-release check are needed.
concerns.quote: just as consistent with a change in contact transparency or contact reconstruction under load (the pressure medium solidifies, the clamp is reloaded)

concerns.concern: The fitted gaps imply 2Δ/kBTc of about 10–13. This is far above weak coupling and above STM and specific-heat estimates, is not discussed, and may indicate spreading resistance stretching the bias axis.
concerns.quote: Such a value is a typical sign of spreading or series resistance stretching the bias axis in partially thermal or diffusive contacts.

concerns.concern: The measured ZBCP height at ambient pressure (about 1.1–1.2) is far below the model's large-Z value (>2). No quantitative explanation is given, and it is not stated whether any scaling or parallel channel was applied.
concerns.quote: The measured G_NS at ambient is ≤1.2. The paper's own Fig. 1c says the ABS peak "readily exceeds 2" at large Z.

concerns.concern: The G(V) normalization procedure is not described, and axes are in arbitrary units, so the headline peak heights used as quantitative criteria cannot be verified. Normalizing near Tc, where a residual hump persists, would distort them.
concerns.quote: The headline peak heights (≈1.2 at ambient, ≈2.08 at 0.8 GPa) therefore cannot be verified.

concerns.concern: Table S1 appears to have Δz and Δx(y) swapped relative to Fig. S7 and the main-text ratio, which affects the key ambient number and the direction of the claimed pz-weight increase.
concerns.quote: The columns appear to be swapped, and this affects the key ambient number.

concerns.concern: The ratio minima used to infer SC2–SC3 transitions rest on few temperature points, have no error bars or statistical test, and are comparable to the scatter at 0 GPa. The 0.8 GPa curve is missing from Fig. S9.
concerns.quote: Any minimum is therefore a dip of 0.05–0.1 in the ratio, defined by 1–3 points.

concerns.concern: Non-monotonic fitted ratios near Tc could be an artifact of the fitting pipeline, because the two gaps become poorly constrained. A synthetic-data refit test is requested.
concerns.quote: Non-monotonic fitted ratios could therefore be an artifact of the fitting procedure.

concerns.concern: Phase boundaries are taken from other groups' measurements on different samples, while the authors' own resistivity shows a single dome and per-pressure Tc is not used. The agreement is therefore partly circular, and calorimetry or susceptibility on S1, or pressure-axis rescaling, is needed.
concerns.quote: Nothing in the paper therefore establishes independently that S1 has multiple superconducting phases at the stated pressures.

concerns.concern: Competing irreps (Au, B1u), s-wave, non-unitary or chiral states and two-band models are excluded only visually, never fitted. Au simulations use much smaller Γ and Δ than the fits, so broadening could merge a split peak into a ZBCP. Quantitative χ²/AIC/BIC comparisons are needed.
concerns.quote: Fit the same spectra with all these models, using the same normalization and the same treatment of Z and Γ. Report reduced χ², AIC/BIC and residuals.

concerns.concern: The fitted Γ falls strongly with pressure for the same contact. The emergence of side dips and the rise of the ZBCP may therefore reflect reduced broadening rather than increased pz weight. The Fig. 4 simulations also use a Γ/Δ smaller than the fits.
concerns.quote: The emergence of side dips and the rise of the ZBCP may therefore reflect reduced broadening rather than increased pz weight.

concerns.concern: The quoted ambient ratio 0.57(5) seems to be a three-sample average, while S1 at 0 and 0.2 GPa are indistinguishable. The claimed abrupt increase rests on a few higher-pressure values without error bars, with no data between 0.2 and 0.6 GPa.
concerns.quote: The "abrupt" increase therefore rests on a few higher-pressure values reported without error bars.

concerns.concern: No manometer or low-temperature pressure calibration is described, and possible clamp-cell pressure loss and non-hydrostaticity of Daphne 7373 are not discussed. It is therefore unclear which phase some pressure points lie in.
concerns.quote: The Methods give no in-situ manometer, such as the Tc of Pb or Sn.

concerns.concern: Kondo or magnetic-scattering origins of the ZBCP are excluded only by the absence of ambient magnetic order. This ignores local moments in a Kondo lattice and spectra taken near the magnetically ordered phases under pressure (1.2–1.4 GPa).
concerns.quote: The authors must state which PCS pressures, if any, lie within or near MO phases, and exclude magnetic-scattering ZBCPs there.

concerns.concern: Field data up to about 8 T exist but only fields below 2 T are discussed, and the field direction is omitted in the caption. The full field dependence should be compared with Hc2, including tests for splitting and field-direction dependence.
concerns.quote: Fig. S2a appears to contain spectra up to about 8 T, yet the text cites only "<2 T."

concerns.concern: The 'nodal' claim is built into the B2u/B3u model. A zero-energy ABS requires only a sign change, and the fully gapped Au simulation also gives side dips. Independent evidence, such as a low-temperature power law in sub-gap conductance, is needed.
concerns.quote: The linear-k B2u/B3u basis has point nodes by construction.

concerns.concern: The SC2 = B2u → SC3 = B3u assignment is not supported by PCS, since the two are indistinguishable on (001); it is imported from NMR. Directional PCS or in-plane field-orientation measurements are needed, otherwise it should be presented as speculative.
concerns.quote: The paper states that B2u and B3u are indistinguishable on (001). The proposed sequence therefore relies entirely on external NMR.

concerns.concern: Within the isotropic model, B2u and B3u give identical (001) spectra, so a B2u→B3u transition should produce no spectral change. A continuous transition would generically produce a two-component state the unitary model cannot describe.
concerns.quote: The model thus predicts no spectral change at a B2u→B3u boundary, yet a minimum in the ratio versus T is interpreted as exactly that transition.

concerns.concern: PCS alone cannot distinguish a thermodynamic phase transition from a crossover, so 'phase transition, not a crossover' is overstated without thermodynamic evidence on the same sample.
concerns.quote: PCS alone does not distinguish a thermodynamic phase transition from a crossover. The wording should be softened

concerns.concern: Z, Γ and the gap parameters are strongly correlated, and quoted uncertainties as small as ±0.01 meV have no stated method and ignore correlations and systematics. Correlation matrices and likelihood or bootstrap contours are requested.
concerns.quote: Quoted uncertainties as small as ±0.01 meV have no stated method.

concerns.concern: The model uses a single spherical Fermi surface with specular reflection, whereas UTe2 has quasi-2D cylindrical sheets that change the angular weighting for (001) injection. The extracted ratio is model-dependent, and refits with realistic Fermi surfaces are needed.
concerns.quote: The authors should refit with a cylindrical Fermi surface, partially diffuse reflection and a tunnelling-cone parameter.

concerns.concern: The superposition model is underspecified: number of channels, shared Z and Γ, weight normalization, irrep of each component, and no statistical criterion such as ΔBIC to justify extra components against overfitting.
concerns.quote: The parameter count grows by about 5 per component, so an information criterion or similar is needed to control overfitting.

concerns.concern: The switch from one-component fits at 0.8 GPa to two-component fits at 1.2 GPa is justified only qualitatively, and the pressure-inhomogeneity explanation is offered without evidence such as transition broadening.
concerns.quote: The "pressure inhomogeneity" explanation is offered without evidence.

concerns.concern: The weighted ratio of summed gaps has no clear physical meaning and may be degenerate in the weights. If components are B2u and B3u, coexistence is assumed, making the SC3 inference partly circular. The ⟨⟩ notation is also used for single-component cases.
concerns.quote: If the components are B2u and B3u, coexistence is already assumed, which makes the later SC3 = B3u inference partly circular.

concerns.concern: The fitted gaps do not close near Tc and Γ/Δ is large, suggesting parameter degeneracy or that the fitted 'gaps' are not the superconducting gap.
concerns.quote: These suggest parameter degeneracy, or that the fitted "gaps" are not the superconducting gap.

concerns.concern: Deviation of Δ(T) from BCS is common in multigap conventional superconductors and sensitive to Γ treatment, so it does not establish unconventional pairing. Fits with fixed and free Γ and alpha-model comparisons are requested.
concerns.quote: Deviation of the fitted Δ(T) from a single BCS curve (Fig. S2c) is common in multigap conventional superconductors.

concerns.concern: The authors' own simulations give only shallow side dips at Γ values like those fitted, so the deep measured dips favour a non-spectroscopic origin.
concerns.quote: deep measured dips at these Γ values are more consistent with a non-spectroscopic origin.

concerns.concern: Triplet pairing is assumed from the outset; even-parity states that change sign under kz → −kz (B2g, B3g) could also produce a ZBCP on (001) and are never considered.
concerns.quote: Even-parity states that change sign under kz → −kz (B2g, B3g, e.g. kxkz) could also produce a ZBCP on (001). They are never considered.

concerns.concern: Lock-in frequency, excitation amplitude and energy resolution are not reported. Modulation and thermal broadening are comparable to the fitted Γ, so Γ cannot be interpreted.
concerns.quote: Modulation broadening of about 0.1 mV and thermal broadening (~0.1 meV at 0.3 K) are comparable to the fitted Γ at high pressure

concerns.concern: Spectra at 1.0 and 1.4 GPa, the latter within the claimed SC3 region and near MO1, are shown but never fitted. The 1.4 GPa flat-topped peak is left uninterpreted, suggesting selective reporting.
concerns.quote: The 1.0 and 1.4 GPa data are never fitted.

concerns.concern: Conflicting reports of a fully gapped ambient state (Suetsugu et al.) and single-component order (Theuss et al.) are not addressed; only agreeing prior work is discussed.
concerns.quote: The paper should also address conflicting reports of a fully gapped ambient state (Suetsugu et al. 2024, Ref. [48]) and of single-component order

concerns.concern: The title and abstract overstate the independent contribution. The paper should clearly separate conclusions from its own data (a model-dependent gap ratio) from those imported from other work.
concerns.quote: the paper clearly separates conclusions drawn from its own data from conclusions imported from other work.

concerns.concern: Novelty should be restricted to measurements under pressure, with an explanation of what PCS adds over bulk probes. The ambient results should be reconciled with prior PCS (Yoon et al., py-dominant) and STM (Gu et al., B3u), including surface preparation.
concerns.quote: The authors call the two results "qualitatively consistent" in a single sentence without reconciling them.

concerns.concern: Claim strength is inconsistent: the text calls the pz/ABS conclusion 'unambiguous' while the abstract says 'strongly suggests', and hedging on the irrep assignment varies across sections.
concerns.quote: The text describes the ABS/pz conclusion as unambiguous, while the abstract says "strongly suggests."

concerns.concern: Surface preparation and contact fabrication are under-documented: no orientation check, polishing damage, natural (011) cleavage, air exposure, or effect of 423 K epoxy curing on the surface.
concerns.quote: There is no Laue or orientation check, and no estimate of misorientation.

concerns.concern: The broad resistive transition (onset 2.6 K, zero resistance 2.1 K) is unusual for RRR ≈ 410 and may indicate filamentary or strained regions, raising doubts about whether PCS probes bulk-representative material. RRR is given only for S1.
concerns.quote: Could this indicate filamentary or strained, possibly surface-near, regions with enhanced Tc?

concerns.concern: Pressure labels are inconsistent across the main text and SI (0.2 vs 0.3 GPa, 0.6/0.8 GPa), which matters because 0.3 GPa lies at a phase boundary. A table of all measured pressures, temperatures, R_N and fit parameters is requested.
concerns.quote: The 0.2 GPa (main text) versus 0.3 GPa (Fig. S3) labelling must also be resolved.

concerns.concern: The pressure at which side dips first appear is stated inconsistently ('above 0.3 GPa' versus emerging at 0.6 GPa).
concerns.quote: The summary says "above 0.3 GPa." The body describes 0.2 GPa as ambient-like, with dips "emerging" at 0.6 GPa.

concerns.concern: It should be shown that the ratio minimum follows the known field dependence of the SC2/SC3 boundary.
concerns.quote: Show that the minimum follows the known field dependence of the SC2/SC3 boundary, e.g. at 0, 0.5 and 1 T at 1.2 GPa.

concerns.concern: The fitting protocol (optimizer, cost function, window, initial values, free versus fixed parameters) is not described. If Z and Γ were fixed in temperature series, all thermal evolution is forced into the gap ratio.
concerns.quote: Their near-constancy suggests they were fixed, which would force all thermal evolution into the gap ratio.

concerns.concern: Simulations treat Γ inconsistently (fixed Γ/Δ in Fig. S5 versus absolute Γ in Fig. S6), making the criteria hard to compare with each other and with the fits.
concerns.quote: Fig. S5 fixes Γ/Δ = 0.2, while Fig. S6 uses absolute Γ (0.00–0.40 meV).

concerns.concern: The zero-energy ABS criterion is stated only for a scalar gap. It should be generalized to multicomponent d-vectors, explaining why Au gives a split peak while B2u gives a zero-bias peak.
concerns.quote: Please generalize it to multicomponent d-vectors.

concerns.concern: The statement that B2u and B3u are indistinguishable appears to follow from the model's in-plane isotropy; this should be stated and a B3u simulation shown.
concerns.quote: This appears to follow from the model's in-plane isotropy. Please state this explicitly.

concerns.concern: The window between Tc0 = 2.1 K and onset Tc = 2.6 K (with a hump at 2.5 K) is not discussed, nor why ambient fits stop at 1.85 K while 0.8 GPa fits extend to 2.1 K.
concerns.quote: A hump is reported at 2.5 K. Please explain how spectral features in this window should be interpreted.

concerns.concern: The topology and Majorana motivation is never connected to the results; the implications of B2u, B3u or two-component states and of pressure tuning are not explained.
concerns.quote: Without this, the significance beyond cataloguing phases is unclear.

concerns.concern: The fitted Δx(y) changes meaning across the transition (Δx → Δy), and reading Δz as 'pz-wave weight' needs justification.
concerns.quote: It should discuss that the fitted quantity "Δx(y)" changes meaning across the transition (Δx → Δy).

concerns.concern: Several quantities needed to reproduce fits are undefined: G0, I0, k∥ weighting and grid, whether d-vector components use k/kF, Δ in Fig. S5, and how Γ enters.
concerns.quote: G0 is described only as "the conductance in the normal state", and I0 in Eq. S10 is undefined.

concerns.concern: The mapping of x, y, z to crystal axes a, b, c is never stated, though irrep labels and field direction depend on it.
concerns.quote: The mapping x, y, z ↔ a, b, c is never stated

concerns.concern: Raw data and fitting code are not available, and the SI link is a placeholder.
concerns.quote: Please deposit raw dI/dV spectra (with R_N) and the BTK and superposition fitting code.

concerns.concern: There are figure and reference errors: mislabelled Fig. S5 panels, inconsistent Fig. S8 temperatures, Ref. 24 misdated, citation lists differing between text and figures, and unsourced SC regions in Fig. S9.
concerns.quote: Figs. S5(a)/(b) appear mislabelled. The panel temperatures in Fig. S8 are inconsistent between text and caption.

concerns.concern: The Au lineshape is described differently in the Fig. 1 caption, main text and SI, and the descriptions should be harmonized.
concerns.quote: The descriptions of the Au signature in the Fig. 1 caption, the main text and the SI are physically equivalent but worded differently.
